svg.text: culture • telemetry • time series • alerts • network • systems • applications • security • SNMP

text.tspan: Collect raw telemetry.
Normalize and retain data.
Evaluate rules, thresholds and history.
Alert, automate or retain for analysis.
Use incidents to improve coverage.
Real-time metrics → thresholds/ranges.
Events → logs and state changes.
Historical trends → time-series context.
High resolution fresh; roll up old data.
Aggregation must fit metric semantics.
Every alert should enable an action.
Define owner and escalation.
Fix false positives instead of ignoring them.
Reserve 24x7 pages for true urgency.
Rotate on-call to reduce burnout.
Threshold: Nagios, Icinga, Sensu.
Time series: Graphite, Prometheus, InfluxDB, Munin.
Visualization: Grafana, Graphite UI.
Choose for sources, UI, cost, reports, integration.
Publication-era product status may be dated.
StatsD transports generic metrics to a backend.
Parse command output only with stable semantics.
df, du, free, iostat, lsof, mpstat, vmstat, sar.
collectd supports continuous daemon-based collection.
sysdig and dtrace provide deeper kernel/process tracing.
Ping proves path and IP-stack response, not app health.
Evaluate packet-loss trend, not one missed probe.
Application metrics require developer/business input.
Logs can become events, rates, alerts and reports.
Useful business metrics may be above OS/network layers.
FIM: trusted baseline → current state → compare.
HIDS and NIDS are detection layers, not complete security.
SNMP model: MIB → OID → get/get-next/set/trap.
Prefer SNMP for specialized/network devices.
snmpset changes state and needs rollback planning.
Monitor hardware signals and every HA member.
Historical data supports RCA, planning and lifecycle work.
Keep documented runbooks for restart/reset/repair.
Monitor the monitoring platform with an independent check.
Every missed failure becomes a new monitoring requirement.
Dependencies and owners identified.
Meaningful metrics/events collected and retained.
Dashboards or query paths exist.
Alerts have owners, escalation and runbooks.
No server or service enters production before monitoring.

svg.text: Core: data is useful only when it supports understanding, action or planning.
Production without monitoring is an operational defect, not a temporary convenience.
